page: Amazon Web Services m6id.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It features 128 vCPUs across 64 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 512 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 7600 GB of NVMe SSD instance store volumes, and it supports a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights strong multi-core capabilities and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Passmark CPU, extended instructions, and encryption tests, alongside top-tier Geekbench ray tracing performance. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and Geekbench is strong, as is memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached read/write operations. Single-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench falls into the average category.

Given its bare-metal nature, high resource density, and substantial local NVMe SSD storage, the m6id.metal offers a highly efficient profile for workloads requiring direct hardware access without hypervisor overhead. The combination of 128 vCPUs, 512 GB of RAM, and 7.6 TB of fast local storage makes it well-suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, containerized microservices, and multi-threaded enterprise applications.
